observations: A dense black ground is divided into horizontal bands by thick yellow arcs and red rectangles, with a large blue rectangle anchoring the lower center.
Repeating spiral forms appear in at least four locations—upper left, upper right, lower left, and center—drawn in yellow, purple, white, and dark outlines at varying scales.
Zigzag border lines in red, pink, and yellow run along the top and bottom edges, while a magenta stepped maze-shape descends through the lower middle third.
reading: The black ground is packed with layered zones of yellow, red, and blue, each edged by zigzag or spiral marks that keep the eye moving rather than settling. Spirals recur at different scales across all four corners, giving the density an internal rhythm. A magenta stepped form drops through the lower center, acting as a hinge between the upper noise and a quieter beige patch below—suggesting pressure without release.
